title: The US House Blocks Pete Hegseth's Impeachment 211-204, Gadi Eisenkot Pushes an October 7 Inquiry as Israel's New Knesset Convenes, and DR Congo's Ebola Death Toll Passes 5,300
subhead: House Republicans voted 211-204 to refer eight impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee even as a Reuters/Ipsos poll showed 71 percent of Americans want Congress to end the Iran war; Israel's opposition-led Knesset was sworn in with coalition formateur Gadi Eisenkot introducing legislation for a state inquiry into the October 7 attacks; and health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported that the country's largest Ebola outbreak has exceeded 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths.

sections.heading: House Blocks Hegseth Impeachment 211-204 as Bessent Relocates Over Iran Threats
sections.body:
The Republican-controlled US House of Representatives voted 211-204 late Tuesday to refer Representative Thomas Massie's eight-article impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, stalling the removal bid for the remainder of the current congressional term (Defense News, BBC, Euronews). Hegseth dismissed the resolution as a 'political farce' and 'sabotage' during his first Pentagon press briefing since May, stating he stands behind every US strike conducted in Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela, while President Donald Trump praised Hegseth and Vice President JD Vance defended the Pentagon chief (Defense News, Times of Israel, Bloomberg HT). A new Reuters/Ipsos poll nevertheless found that 71 percent of Americans want the incoming Democratic-majority Congress to pass legislation ending the war with Iran and rolling back tariffs (Defense News, TRT Haber).

Security protocols inside the administration tightened further as US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was reportedly moved to a military base residence following intelligence warnings of Iranian threats against his life, coinciding with a Justice Department indictment of three Iranian nationals on federal terrorism charges (CNBC). Simultaneously, a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) deportation charter flight carrying Iranian detainees to Pakistan for onward transfer to Tehran turned back mid-route and landed in Arizona following emergency legal intervention (New York Times). Ahead of the new legislative term, House Republicans elected Representative Jim Jordan as their conference leader while Senator John Thune retained the Senate Republican leadership post, even as incoming Ohio Democratic Representative-elect Don Leonard alleged party leaders threatened him over withholding support for Hakeem Jeffries' speakership bid (Dünya, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Referring Hegseth's impeachment resolution to committee by a seven-vote margin only postpones the confrontation until January, when a new Democratic majority takes the gavel backed by 71 percent public support for ending the Iran conflict.

sections.heading: Israel's New Knesset Convenes With Oct. 7 Inquiry Push as US Senators Challenge NDAA Clauses
sections.body:
Dozens of newly elected lawmakers were sworn into Israel's parliament on Tuesday as the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot assumed a parliamentary majority following the October 27 election (New York Times, DW). Although Eisenkot has not yet finalized a governing coalition to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, he pledged immediate legislative action—starting with a bill to establish an independent state commission of inquiry with subpoena powers to investigate government failures surrounding the October 7, 2023 attacks (Le Monde, New York Times). The opening session descended into shouting matches as former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett repeatedly heckled Netanyahu from the floor and the Arab-led Joint List condemned Netanyahu's speech as 'racism and hysteria' (Al Jazeera, Star).

In Washington, 12 Democratic senators sent a formal letter to congressional leadership demanding the removal of three provisions in the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would expand US-Israeli defense integration and intelligence sharing, while Representative Delia Ramirez said she discussed scheduling a floor vote on the 'Block the Bombs Act' with top House Democrats after President Trump moved to end annual US military grant aid to Israel under Section 219 (Star, Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera). Along Israel's northern border, the UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon (UNIFIL) reported that one of its patrols came under small-arms fire of roughly a dozen rounds and returned fire (CNA).
sections.whyItMatters: With an opposition majority now seated in the Knesset, Eisenkot can pass a statutory October 7 inquiry into Netanyahu's conduct by simple majority even before completing formal coalition talks.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi Talks Enter Day Two as Zelensky Signals Readiness to Discuss Territory
sections.body:
Delegations from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States opened a second day of trilateral ceasefire negotiations in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday after Washington proposed a new European security arrangement on day one (France 24, AFP). Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed what he called positive adjustments in the American mediation team's approach and stated publicly that Kyiv is prepared for leader-level talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin mediated by the US and Europe, adding, 'We are ready to sit down and discuss the territorial issue' (AFP, France 24, Star). On the margins of G7 meetings in Paris, Ukrainian and South Korean foreign ministers also met to discuss normalizing ties following recent tensions over North Korean prisoners of war (Anadolu Agency).

Despite the talks in the Emirates, long-range strikes escalated across Northern and Eastern Europe. Western and Ukrainian officials estimated that Ukrainian drone strikes have now reduced Russia's oil refining capacity by 30 percent, while Russia's defense ministry claimed it intercepted 146 Ukrainian drones overnight over the Leningrad region near Baltic Sea oil terminals (The Independent, Al Jazeera, Dünya). Air raid alerts sent residents near the Belarusian border in Latvia and Lithuania into shelters as NATO fighters scrambled, while British counterterrorism police arrested a 41-year-old senior US soldier in London on suspicion of spying for Russia (Le Monde, Defense News, NTV, Star).
sections.whyItMatters: Zelensky's explicit statement that Kyiv is ready to discuss territorial issues marks a major rhetorical shift aimed at keeping Washington aligned with Ukraine during the Abu Dhabi negotiations.

sections.heading: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Passes 5,300 Deaths and South Korea Fines Bond Dealers 1.6T Won
sections.body:
Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported that the country's worst-ever Ebola epidemic has surpassed 11,000 confirmed and probable cases with at least 5,387 deaths, as ongoing militia fighting in the eastern provinces and delayed diagnostic detection hamper containment teams (Al Jazeera). In the Caribbean, Trinidad and Tobago's highest court unanimously struck down a colonial-era law criminalizing same-sex relations, ruling that the ban violated constitutional guarantees of privacy and individual liberty (Le Monde).

Across Asia-Pacific financial markets, South Korea's antitrust regulator fined 15 major bond houses a combined 1.6 trillion won for colluding on government bond yields, while a morning rush-hour crash in Seongnam south of Seoul—in which a passenger bus plowed into 32 vehicles—left at least 57 people injured (CNA, DW, Anadolu Agency). In Japan, surging yields lured household savers back into fixed income, doubling monthly issuance of retail Japanese government bonds as returns reached 2.39 percent, while in Australia, 188-year-old department store chain David Jones announced plans to close half its stores after entering voluntary administration (Financial Times, The Guardian).
sections.whyItMatters: An Ebola outbreak exceeding 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths in conflict-hit eastern Congo risks cross-border transmission into neighboring Great Lakes states unless international medical access is secured.

bottomLine: Overnight developments underscored deep political and security transitions from Washington to Jerusalem and Abu Dhabi: House Republicans voted 211-204 to refer Pete Hegseth's impeachment resolution to committee even as 71 percent of Americans polled backed ending the Iran war and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base over Iranian threats. In Jerusalem, an opposition majority took control of the Knesset as Gadi Eisenkot pushed an October 7 state inquiry, while in Abu Dhabi, Ukraine and Russia entered a second day of US-mediated talks with President Zelensky signaling readiness to discuss territorial questions. Meanwhile, DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 11,000 cases and 5,387 deaths, UK police arrested a US soldier suspected of spying for Russia, and South Korea fined 15 bond dealers 1.6 trillion won for collusion.
sources: Reuters, AFP, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, New York Times, CNBC, BBC, The Guardian, Le Monde, Al Jazeera, DW, France 24, Euronews, CNA, SCMP, Times of Israel, Defense News, Anadolu Agency, TRT Haber, NTV, Dünya, Star
